narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus encounters Achilles among the dead and praises his status. Achilles answers by preferring even a poor living servant’s life to rule among the dead. The exchange tests the value of glory against the loss of life.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “are dead.’ “‘Say not a word,’ he answered, ‘in death’s favour; I would rather be a paid servant in a poor man’s house and be above ground than king of kings among the dead. But give me news about my son; is he gone to the wars and will he be a great soldier, or is this not so? Tell me also if you have”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The dead return memory, grief, and unfinished obligation. Glory looks different when the people who paid for it can speak.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Hear Achilles’ reply before summarising the episode as praise of fame. His preference for humble life puts pressure on Odysseus’ attempt to console him with status among the dead.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: This prepares you to compare other underworld journeys as encounters with a tradition's memory system.

quiz.prompt: How does the dead Achilles respond to praise of his status?

choices.text: He asks Odysseus to win another war for him.
He says death has fulfilled every heroic wish.
He says he would rather be alive in humble service.
